title: Create an Excel table with AI from a specific range
h1: make a real excel table from the range you choose
description: Ask a bot to turn an Excel worksheet range into a table. Confirm the workbook, sheet, address and header row before it makes the change.
keywords: claude convert range to excel table
ai create table in excel worksheet
answer: **turn the pasted cells into a proper excel table without typing them again.** a bot wraps the existing range in a table. give it the workbook, sheet and cells, then say whether the first row holds column names. you get the same data in a table, with the report title and footnotes left outside.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: a table with its boundaries agreed.
what:
**the table should start at your column names and end at your last record.** the bot finds the workbook in onedrive and reads the cells first. it creates a table over existing data; it adds no new rows.

name the sheet and range, such as `a1:d4` on intake. say whether that first row contains headers. that keeps a real record from becoming a heading.
uses: **tidy a visitor log.** turn its entries and column names into a table.
**prepare pasted orders.** turn the existing cells into a table before sharing the workbook.
**keep the title outside.** start a supplier contact table below the report heading.

routine.message:
on the first monday of each month at 10, inspect the new monthly intake sheet in the cloudbridge permits workbook.

- show the proposed range around intake columns only
- say whether its first row contains headers
- ask me before you change anything

after i agree, create the table and report the sheet and range here. exclude notes beneath the data. leave cell values alone. if a table already exists there, stop instead of making another.
routine.when: first monday of the month at 10:00
routine.needs: excel connected with read and write; access to the cloudbridge permits workbook
routine.output:
cloudbridge permits
sheet: november intake
range: a3:e18
headers in the first selected row: yes
notes below row 18 stay outside.
proposed table: november intake, a3:e18. approve that range to create it.

steps: **allow table creation.** connect excel with read and write for this bot.
**find the workbook.** give its name and have the bot show which sheet it found.
**draw the boundary.** ask for the range and header choice before creation.
**inspect the result.** open the workbook after creation. pause the monthly job if its layout changes.
watch: **cells need a sheet.** name it separately or include it in the range address.
**start below the report title.** the first table row should contain column names or data, as you chose.
**use a separate import to add rows.** table creation wraps the cells already there.
**keep creation behind your go-ahead.** the sending rule does not cover tables; the routine above tells the bot to wait.

faq.q: do i need to type the data again?
faq.a: **no, keep the existing cells.** this action creates a table around them. it takes no new row values.

faq.q: what if the report title sits above my column names?
faq.a: **start at the column names.** say that row contains headers and check the range before creation.

steps: connect excel with read and write
name a workbook, sheet and a small range
ask for a range preview, with no changes
open excel and confirm the selected top row contains column names

worked.intro: invented example: harriet turns a monthly intake sheet into a table.
worked.before: a report title sits above a3:e18. notes begin below row 18. selecting everything would mix three different things.
worked.after: the bot proposes a3:e18, with headers. harriet approves that range. the table holds the intake records; the title and notes stay outside.

items: the workbook and sheet are right
the range starts at the column names
notes sit outside the selected cells
no table already occupies that range

mistakes.fix: choose the data and its column names. leave titles and footnotes outside.

mistakes.mistake: expecting an approval card for a table
mistakes.fix: require a preview and your go-ahead in the request. table creation does not use the send setting.

tip.text: footnotes make terrible table records. stop the range at the last entry.
